text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Preparations for establishing a new Central Bank in Bosnia have started. The working group, including representatives of Bosnia's National Bank, National Bank of Serb Republic and finance ministries of Bosnia's Federation and Serb entities, has been instructed to prepare a draft law on the new central bank by the end of October.

- According to the Dayton Peace Accords, a new central bank should issue new domestic currency and operate currency board, says Michael Maclay, spokesman for the Office of the High Representative to Bosnia.

- Kresimir Zubak, president of the Moslem-Croat Federation and Croat member of the new three-man Bosnian Presidency, met international officals based in Bosnia to discuss logistics and preparations for upcoming municipal elections.
- Due to P-2 form, majority of Bosnia's electorate has been improperly "moved" into Serb Republic, says Kasim Begic, Bosnian member of the OSCE's Provisional Election Commission.
- A number of employed people in Bosnia rose 0.9 per cent in July, according to Bosnia's statistics bureau.
- Five-member coalition "Joint List" will not participate in Bosnia's municipal elections if irregularities spotted in general elections are not removed.
- Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic denies "Washington Post" report about presence of foreign Islamic "mujahideen" forces in Bosnia.
